nfl.ot_model.mechanism: Overtime frequency, the overtime rule set in force that season and tie probability determine settlement of regulation-only versus including-OT markets. From 2025 the regular-season overtime is a single 10-minute period in which both teams get a possession (an opening-drive touchdown no longer ends the game), then sudden death; the game is a tie if the period expires level. Seasons 2017-2024 used the 10-minute first-possession-touchdown-wins format; the playoffs have no time limit.
nfl.ot_model.measurement: P(tie after 60 min) from the model margin lattice mass at 0 (nfl.model_margin_lattice, own means, no betting lines). Overtime: drive simulation under the rule era of the season (2017-2024: first-possession TD wins, 10 min; 2025+: both teams possess unless the first drive consumes the full 10 minutes and scores, then sudden death, 10 min; playoffs: both possess, untimed). Per drive, outcome rates (TD, FG, punt/turnover, safety) and drive duration from the two teams' own drive model by field position, shrunk to league with k=150 drives. A TD that wins outright ends the game with no try; a try follows only a TD that does not end it (first-possession TD, or a second-team TD that ties or trails), with the extra-point versus two-point choice by coach and score state. Resulting final margins: 6 or 3 for a second-team TD or FG after nothing/FG; 3, 4, 5 for a FG answered against a TD+try of 6, 7, 8; 1 or 2 after a matching TD and try; 6-8 for an unanswered TD; sudden death 3 (FG), 6 (TD), 2 (safety). Output P(OT), P(win | OT) per team, the OT points distribution, and P(level after OT) per game, refitted by era (2012-2016, 2017-2024, 2025+); use settlement wording to decide which components to include.

nfl.ot_ending_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the overtime period fails to produce a decisive score under the rule era in force: from 2025 in the regular season both teams get a possession inside a 10-minute period followed by sudden death, so a level finish needs equal scores (no score, matched FGs, matched TDs and tries) when the clock expires.
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.measurement: Simulate OT as a drive process with a 10-minute clock (regular season) and the possession rule of the season's era (2017-2024 first-possession TD wins; 2025+ both teams possess unless the opening drive uses the full period and scores, then sudden death); per drive TD/FG/safety/empty rates and drive duration from the two teams' drive-level data shrunk to league with k=150 drives; a try only after a TD that does not end the game (walk-off TDs have none), with extra-point versus two-point choice from coach policy; 4th-down aggression. Level outcome = period expires with equal scores (no score, matched FGs, matched TD plus equal try). Calibrate to realized regular-season OT outcomes per era since 2012; report P(level | OT) with credible interval; as-of start of season and refreshed weekly.

nfl.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: Each off-field series is priced from a named reference class of comparable past events with its historical frequency by calendar window: head-coach exits and hires, trades, retirements and roster events from the transaction history, cross-sport athletes linked to an NFL signing for the celebrity series, and announced international games for the game-location series.
nfl.offfield_base_rate.rationale: Off-field markets are not game-model problems; the prior is the historical frequency of a defined class conditional on record, contract and calendar, updated by dated official reporting. Classes must be declared per series: a celebrity-signing market has almost no successes in its class, so the prior is near zero and dominated by verified tryout or signing news, while ownership-stake and stadium-completion series are out of scope and excluded rather than given an invented prior.
nfl.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Per series reference class, window and estimator. (1) Coach exit/hire (KXNFLCOACHOUT, KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT, KXNFLHIRECOACH): head-coach seasons 2000-2025, event by calendar week, conditioned on win% bin and tenure, Gamma-Poisson shrinkage (prior shape 2, rate 4 team-years). (2) Trades, next team, retirement, 53-man (KXNFLTRADE, KXNFLNEXTTEAM, KXNFLRETIRE, KXNFL53MAN): transaction log 2010-2025 by type and week, conditioned on contract year and age, same shrinkage. (3) Cross-sport athlete signing or snap (KXNFLHKANE, KXNFLCOMPETE): class = non-NFL athletes publicly reported as working out for or negotiating with an NFL team 2000-2025 (International Player Pathway rugby and other athletes, soccer and track converts, celebrities); success = official signing (HKANE) or a recorded snap (COMPETE) within the contract window; Beta(0.5, 0.5) prior updated by class counts, then multiplied by 0.1 when no credible tryout or negotiation report exists for the named person. (4) International game venue retention (KXNFLGAMELOCATION): announced international regular-season games 2007-2025, share played in the announced city by the announced date, Beta(1,1) prior. Excluded: KXNFLOWNERSTAKE and KXNFLSTADIUM, re-filed OUT_OF_SCOPE in the final series assignment. Store each event's official announcement timestamp; as-of quote time.
raw_data: coach seasons: team, coach, start/end dates, win%
transaction log: date, player, team, type
cross-sport athlete list: name, sport, first NFL report date, signing date, snap date
international games: announced city, announcement date, played city and date

nfl.vote_outcome_model.mechanism: Winner or rank probability from candidate quality, narrative, previous votes, timing and electorate composition, aggregated through each award's actual ballot: AP MVP since 2022 is a 50-voter top-5 ranked ballot scored 10-5-3-2-1, other AP awards and Coach of the Year a top-3 ballot scored 5-3-1, earlier seasons a single first-place vote.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.measurement: Per AP award, model each voter's ranked ballot: rank-ordered (exploded) logit of candidate placements on features (team win% at ballot close, statistical rank within position by EPA or season totals, prior award wins, position dummy), ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, prior weight 3 pseudo-observations; fit 2022-2025 on full placement counts (MVP 5 places, others 3) and pre-2022 on first-place votes only as a separate regime sharing feature weights through a hierarchical prior. Simulate 50 ballots per draw, score with 10-5-3-2-1 (MVP) or 5-3-1 (other AP awards), winner = highest points (ties shared). Non-AP processes (PFWA Executive of the Year, Hall of Fame, All-Pro, T100) keep their own model: T100 ordered logit on previous rank, change in production, position group, age. Output P(candidate=winner) and P(rank=r); group markets P(group) = sum of P(win) by team at announcement time with 1/N co-winner payout; Executive of the Year tie probability = own-award co-winner frequency shrunk to comparable awards with weight 10. As-of ballot close.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.mechanism: Reduction in a candidate's ballot placements caused by another strong candidate with the same team, position or narrative; under ranked-points ballots it acts mostly on first-place share, because both rivals can still collect lower-place points.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: Since 2022 AP awards are ranked-points ballots (MVP 10-5-3-2-1 over five places, other AP awards 5-3-1 over three), so two similar candidates split first places but not all support: a candidate can win on second- and third-place points (2025 MVP: Stafford 366 points with 24 firsts, Maye 361 with 23). A penalty fitted to first-place shares under plurality overstates the split for ranked seasons and must be estimated by regime.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: Rank-ordered logit latent utility for candidate i on voter ballot = x_i'theta - beta_r x max over same-team or same-position rivals j of x_j'theta, where x are the nfl.vote_outcome_model features and r indexes the placement (first place versus lower places). Estimate theta and beta_r by maximum likelihood on placement counts per candidate for 2022-2025 ranked seasons (MVP five places, other AP awards three), and on first-place vote shares under a Dirichlet-multinomial for 2005-2021 single-vote seasons as a separate regime; ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, shrink beta_r toward 0. Output winner probabilities from simulated 50-voter ballots scored by the award's point scheme. As-of ballot close.
raw_data: AP vote tallies by candidate-season: points and placement counts (2022+), first-place votes (pre-2022)

nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.mechanism: Estimates the dependence between the two teams' scores through shared pace, shared weather and the score path and outputs their joint integer pmf, from which the single-team conditional pmf (team totals), the both-teams-at-least-N tail (game_total's KXNFLBOTH) and the game-total tail (slate extremes) are read.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.rationale: Team scores are positively correlated through plays and drives and conditionally negative through script (a leading team slows play and shortens the other side's comeback window). The sign and size vary by expected total and weather, so any contract on one team conditioned on the game, on both teams' tails or on the sum needs the joint pmf rather than a product of marginals; the dependence is strongest in the high-total tail.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.measurement: Using 2010-2025 regular-season games, compute residuals of (home score - own model home mean) and (away score - own model away mean), where means are walk-forward outputs of nfl.model_team_points_mean including the home shift and dome flag. Bins: expected total (<40, 40-50, >50 model points) x wind (<10, 10-15, >=15 mph; roofed games count as calm), 9 cells. Per cell fit a Student-t copula on the probability-integral transforms of the two scores (correlation rho_b and degrees of freedom nu_b in 2..30 by maximum likelihood), shrinking rho_b toward the pooled value with weight n_b/(n_b+150) and log(nu_b) toward pooled with the same weight; upper-tail dependence lambda_U follows from (rho_b, nu_b). Simulate pairs from the copula and map each margin through that team's nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean marginal (OT-inclusive or regulation-only per contract). Tail check: compare simulated and empirical P(both >= N) for N = 28, 35, 42 per bin on held-out seasons. Output the joint pmf P(home=h, away=a) for h, a in 0..70, rho_b, nu_b and lambda_U per cell; consumers read P(team>=n | game draw), P(both>=N) and P(home+away>=T). As-of kickoff weather forecast and model means; no betting total used.

nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.label: Yearly Combine best marks by drill (40, broad jump, vertical, bench reps) and record tail
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.mechanism: Distribution of the yearly fastest 40, longest broad jump, highest vertical and most bench-press reps across classes, used to calibrate the extreme-value tail of each drill and the chance of breaking its record.
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.measurement: From nflverse Combine data 2006-2025 (fixed window; earlier timing regime excluded), take each year's best 40 time (minimum), broad jump (maximum, inches), vertical (maximum, inches) and bench press (maximum reps at 225 lb) among participants. For the three continuous drills fit a GEV to the 20 yearly maxima (sign-flipped for the 40) with location mu = a + b x (season-2006) + c x ln(number of participants who recorded the drill); shape by maximum likelihood with a Normal(0, 0.15) prior. For bench reps (integer) fit the same GEV to yearly maxima and discretise by rounding with continuity correction. Parametric bootstrap 2,000 draws for intervals. Output P(max >= x) for any strike and the distribution of the winning mark per drill. As-of before testing, using the forecast participant count per drill.
raw_data: combine.season, player, pos, forty, broad_jump, vertical, bench
participant counts by drill, position and year

nfl.ot_total_increment.mechanism: Points added to a full-game total by overtime and the probability of reaching overtime, by season rule era; under the 2025+ both-possess regular-season format both teams can score in OT, so increments such as 9, 10, 13, 14, 16 and 17 occur beside 3 and 6.
nfl.ot_total_increment.rationale: If overtime counts for the contract, the total shifts by the OT points only in games tied after regulation; the rule era sets which OT score paths are possible (2017-2024 a first-possession TD ended the game, from 2025 both teams possess in a 10-minute period), so the increment distribution must be simulated per era and not taken from pooled history or from betting lines.
nfl.ot_total_increment.measurement: P(OT) per game = mass at margin 0 of nfl.model_margin_lattice (own means, no betting spread or total). OT points distribution = sum of both teams' OT points from the drive simulation of nfl.ot_model under the season's rule era (try only after a non-ending TD; walk-off TDs score 6), with per-drive outcome rates shrunk to league (k=150 drives); validate against realized qtr-5 points in nflverse pbp per era (2012-2016, 2017-2024, 2025+). Output P(OT), E[OT points] and the OT-points pmf, and the shift of P(total > strike) when OT counts. As-of start of week.
raw_data: pbp: qtr==5 scoring plays, drive results, game result
